sample.question:
Balance Scale is a weighing-deduction puzzle. The picture shows several two-pan balance scales, numbered under their bases. Every fruit of the same kind always has the same hidden weight, and different kinds may have different weights. A scale whose green pointer is centered and whose beam is level is EXACTLY balanced: its two pans carry equal total weight. A scale with a red pointer is tilted: the lower pan is strictly heavier. Iron blocks are labeled with their exact mass in kg.

Look at the tilted scale (Scale 5): its left pan hangs lower, so that side is heavier. You may move EXACTLY ONE fruit from the left (heavier) pan over to the right pan. Which move makes the scale balance exactly?

Options:
[1] Move one apple to the right pan
[2] Move one orange to the right pan
[3] Move one pear to the right pan
[4] No single fruit move can balance this scale
sample.analysis:
First deduce every fruit's weight from the balanced scales:
Scale 2 balances 2 apples against 3 pears. In units of one apple, the left pan weighs 2 x apple = 2 apple(s), so 3 pear(s) = 2 apple(s), giving 1 pear = 2/3 apple(s).
Scale 3 balances 2 apples against 1 banana. In units of one apple, the left pan weighs 2 x apple = 2 apple(s), so 1 banana(s) = 2 apple(s), giving 1 banana = 2 apple(s).
Scale 4 balances 4 apples against 3 oranges. In units of one apple, the left pan weighs 4 x apple = 4 apple(s), so 3 orange(s) = 4 apple(s), giving 1 orange = 4/3 apple(s).
Scale 1 balances 1 banana + 1 orange against a 10 kg iron weight. In units of one apple the left pan weighs 1 x 2 + 1 x 4/3 = 10/3 apple(s), so 10/3 x weight(apple) = 10 kg, giving weight(apple) = 3 kg.
So the weights are: apple = 3 kg, banana = 6 kg, orange = 4 kg, pear = 2 kg.
On Scale 5, the left pan (2 apples + 1 orange + 1 pear) weighs 12 kg and the right pan (2 apples) weighs 6 kg; the difference is 6 kg. Moving a fruit of weight w changes the difference by 2w, so we need 2w = 6, i.e. w = 3 kg.
Moving one apple (3 kg): heavier pan becomes 12 - 3 = 9 kg, lighter pan becomes 6 + 3 = 9 kg -> balances.
Moving one orange (4 kg): heavier pan becomes 12 - 4 = 8 kg, lighter pan becomes 6 + 4 = 10 kg -> gives 8 kg vs 10 kg - still unbalanced.
Moving one pear (2 kg): heavier pan becomes 12 - 2 = 10 kg, lighter pan becomes 6 + 2 = 8 kg -> gives 10 kg vs 8 kg - still unbalanced.
Only moving one apple works. The option number is 1.

Move one pear to the right pan
